title: The journey to Jerusalem + Agabus's prophecy and Paul's arrest in the temple

paragraphs.text: And when it came to pass that were parted from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course unto Cos, and the next day unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, εὐθυδρομήσαντες ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν Κῶ, τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον, κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Πάταρα·
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de egeneto anachthēnai hēmas apospasthentas apʼ autōn, euthydromēsantes ēlthomen eis tēn Kō, tē de hexēs eis tēn Rhodon, kakeithen eis Patara·

paragraphs.text: and having found a ship crossing over unto Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set sail.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὑρόντες πλοῖον διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην ἐπιβάντες ἀνήχθημεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai heurontes ploion diaperōn eis Phoinikēn epibantes anēchthēmen.

paragraphs.text: And when we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed unto Syria, and landed at Tyre; for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
paragraphs.original: ἀναφάναντες δὲ τὴν Κύπρον καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον ἐπλέομεν εἰς Συρίαν, καὶ κατήλθομεν εἰς Τύρον, ἐκεῖσε γὰρ τὸ πλοῖον ἦν ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον.
paragraphs.translit: anaphanantes de tēn Kypron kai katalipontes autēn euōnymon epleomen eis Syrian, kai katēlthomen eis Tyron, ekeise gar to ploion ēn apophortizomenon ton gomon.

paragraphs.text: And having found the disciples, we tarried there seven days: and these said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not set foot in Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: ἀνευρόντες δὲ τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐπεμείναμεν αὐτοῦ ἡμέρας ἑπτά, οἵτινες τῷ Παύλῳ ἔλεγον διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος μὴ ἐπιβαίνειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: aneurontes de tous mathētas epemeinamen autou hēmeras hepta, hoitines tō Paulō elegon dia tou pneumatos mē epibainein eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: And when it came to pass that we had accomplished the days, we departed and went on our journey; and they all, with wives and children, brought us on our way till we were out of the city: and kneeling down on the beach, we prayed, and bade each other farewell;
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐξαρτίσαι ἡμᾶς τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐξελθόντες ἐπορευόμεθα προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων σὺν γυναιξὶ καὶ τέκνοις ἕως ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν προσευξάμενοι
paragraphs.translit: hote de egeneto exartisai hēmas tas hēmeras, exelthontes eporeuometha propempontōn hēmas pantōn syn gynaixi kai teknois heōs exō tēs poleōs, kai thentes ta gonata epi ton aigialon proseuxamenoi

paragraphs.text: and we went on board the ship, but they returned home again.
paragraphs.original: ἀπησπασάμεθα ἀλλήλους, καὶ ἐνέβημεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὰ ἴδια.
paragraphs.translit: apēspasametha allēlous, kai enebēmen eis to ploion, ekeinoi de hypestrepsan eis ta idia.

paragraphs.text: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais; and we saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
paragraphs.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸν πλοῦν διανύσαντες ἀπὸ Τύρου κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα, καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἐμείναμεν ἡμέραν μίαν παρʼ αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Hēmeis de ton ploun dianysantes apo Tyrou katēntēsamen eis Ptolemaida, kai aspasamenoi tous adelphous emeinamen hēmeran mian parʼ autois.

paragraphs.text: And on the morrow we departed, and came unto Caesarea: and entering into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we abode with him.
paragraphs.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντες ἤλθομεν εἰς Καισάρειαν, καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φιλίππου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐμείναμεν παρʼ αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: tē de epaurion exelthontes ēlthomen eis Kaisareian, kai eiselthontes eis ton oikon Philippou tou euangelistou ontos ek tōn hepta emeinamen parʼ autō.

paragraphs.text: Now this man had four virgin daughters, who prophesied.
paragraphs.original: τούτῳ δὲ ἦσαν θυγατέρες τέσσαρες παρθένοι προφητεύουσαι.
paragraphs.translit: toutō de ēsan thygateres tessares parthenoi prophēteuousai.

paragraphs.text: And as we tarried there some days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιμενόντων δὲ ἡμέρας πλείους κατῆλθέν τις ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας προφήτης ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος,
paragraphs.translit: epimenontōn de hēmeras pleious katēlthen tis apo tēs Ioudaias prophētēs onomati Hagabos,

paragraphs.text: And coming to us, and taking Paul`s girdle, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, Thus saith the Holy Spirit, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου δήσας ἑαυτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Τάδε λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον Τὸν ἄνδρα οὗ ἐστιν ἡ ζώνη αὕτη, οὕτως δήσουσιν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elthōn pros hēmas kai aras tēn zōnēn tou Paulou dēsas heautou tous podas kai tas cheiras eipen· Tade legei to pneuma to hagion Ton andra hou estin hē zōnē hautē, houtōs dēsousin en Ierousalēm hoi Ioudaioi kai paradōsousin eis cheiras ethnōn.

paragraphs.text: And when we heard these things, both we and they of that place besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἠκούσαμεν ταῦτα, παρεκαλοῦμεν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἐντόπιοι τοῦ μὴ ἀναβαίνειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de ēkousamen tauta, parekaloumen hēmeis te kai hoi entopioi tou mē anabainein auton eis Ierousalēm.

paragraphs.text: Then Paul answered, What do ye, weeping and breaking my heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Παῦλος· Τί ποιεῖτε κλαίοντες καὶ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν; ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐ μόνον δεθῆναι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀποθανεῖν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἑτοίμως ἔχω ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tote apekrithē ho Paulos· Ti poieite klaiontes kai synthryptontes mou tēn kardian; egō gar ou monon dethēnai alla kai apothanein eis Ierousalēm hetoimōs echō hyper tou onomatos tou kyriou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
paragraphs.original: μὴ πειθομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡσυχάσαμεν εἰπόντες· Τοῦ κυρίου τὸ θέλημα γινέσθω.
paragraphs.translit: mē peithomenou de autou hēsychasamen eipontes· Tou kyriou to thelēma ginesthō.

paragraphs.text: And after these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας ἐπισκευασάμενοι ἀνεβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα·
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tas hēmeras tautas episkeuasamenoi anebainomen eis Hierosolyma·

paragraphs.text: And there went with us also [certain] of the disciples from Caesarea, bringing [with them] one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we should lodge.
paragraphs.original: συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν ἀπὸ Καισαρείας σὺν ἡμῖν, ἄγοντες παρʼ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν Μνάσωνί τινι Κυπρίῳ, ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ.
paragraphs.translit: synēlthon de kai tōn mathētōn apo Kaisareias syn hēmin, agontes parʼ hō xenisthōmen Mnasōni tini Kypriō, archaiō mathētē.

paragraphs.text: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
paragraphs.original: Γενομένων δὲ ἡμῶν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀσμένως ἀπεδέξαντο ἡμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοί.
paragraphs.translit: Genomenōn de hēmōn eis Hierosolyma asmenōs apedexanto hēmas hoi adelphoi.

paragraphs.text: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
paragraphs.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰσῄει ὁ Παῦλος σὺν ἡμῖν πρὸς Ἰάκωβον, πάντες τε παρεγένοντο οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.
paragraphs.translit: tē de epiousē eisēei ho Paulos syn hēmin pros Iakōbon, pantes te paregenonto hoi presbyteroi.

paragraphs.text: And when he had saluted them, he rehearsed one by one the things which God had wrought among the Gentiles through his ministry.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀσπασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐξηγεῖτο καθʼ ἓν ἕκαστον ὧν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai aspasamenos autous exēgeito kathʼ hen hekaston hōn epoiēsen ho theos en tois ethnesin dia tēs diakonias autou.

paragraphs.text: And they, when they heard it, glorified God; and they said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of them that have believed; and they are all zealous for the law:
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, εἶπόν τε αὐτῷ· Θεωρεῖς, ἀδελφέ, πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσὶν ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τῶν πεπιστευκότων, καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τοῦ νόμου ὑπάρχουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de akousantes edoxazon ton theon, eipon te autō· Theōreis, adelphe, posai myriades eisin en tois Ioudaiois tōn pepisteukotōn, kai pantes zēlōtai tou nomou hyparchousin·

paragraphs.text: and they have been informed concerning thee, that thou teachest all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children neither to walk after the customs.
paragraphs.original: κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάντας Ἰουδαίους, λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσιν περιπατεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: katēchēthēsan de peri sou hoti apostasian didaskeis apo Mōyseōs tous kata ta ethnē pantas Ioudaious, legōn mē peritemnein autous ta tekna mēde tois ethesin peripatein.

paragraphs.text: What is it therefore? They will certainly hear that thou art come.
paragraphs.original: τί οὖν ἐστιν; πάντως ἀκούσονται ὅτι ἐλήλυθας.
paragraphs.translit: ti oun estin; pantōs akousontai hoti elēlythas.

paragraphs.text: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men that have a vow on them;
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο οὖν ποίησον ὅ σοι λέγομεν· εἰσὶν ἡμῖν ἄνδρες τέσσαρες εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: touto oun poiēson ho soi legomen· eisin hēmin andres tessares euchēn echontes aphʼ heautōn.

paragraphs.text: these take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges for them, that they may shave their heads: and all shall know that there is no truth in the things whereof they have been informed concerning thee; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, keeping the law.
paragraphs.original: τούτους παραλαβὼν ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς ἵνα ξυρήσονται τὴν κεφαλήν, καὶ γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ὧν κατήχηνται περὶ σοῦ οὐδέν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖς καὶ αὐτὸς φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον.
paragraphs.translit: toutous paralabōn hagnisthēti syn autois kai dapanēson epʼ autois hina xyrēsontai tēn kephalēn, kai gnōsontai pantes hoti hōn katēchēntai peri sou ouden estin, alla stoicheis kai autos phylassōn ton nomon.

paragraphs.text: But as touching the Gentiles that have believed, we wrote, giving judgment that they should keep themselves from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication.
paragraphs.original: περὶ δὲ τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἐθνῶν ἡμεῖς ἀπεστείλαμεν κρίναντες φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς τό τε εἰδωλόθυτον καὶ αἷμα καὶ πνικτὸν καὶ πορνείαν.
paragraphs.translit: peri de tōn pepisteukotōn ethnōn hēmeis apesteilamen krinantes phylassesthai autous to te eidōlothyton kai haima kai pnikton kai porneian.

paragraphs.text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them went into the temple, declaring the fulfilment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.
paragraphs.original: τότε ὁ Παῦλος παραλαβὼν τοὺς ἄνδρας τῇ ἐχομένῃ ἡμέρᾳ σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς εἰσῄει εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, διαγγέλλων τὴν ἐκπλήρωσιν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ ἁγνισμοῦ ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου αὐτῶν ἡ προσφορά.
paragraphs.translit: tote ho Paulos paralabōn tous andras tē echomenē hēmera syn autois hagnistheis eisēei eis to hieron, diangellōn tēn ekplērōsin tōn hēmerōn tou hagnismou heōs hou prosēnechthē hyper henos hekastou autōn hē prosphora.

paragraphs.text: And when the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι, οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι θεασάμενοι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ συνέχεον πάντα τὸν ὄχλον καὶ ἐπέβαλον ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας,
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de emellon hai hepta hēmerai synteleisthai, hoi apo tēs Asias Ioudaioi theasamenoi auton en tō hierō synecheon panta ton ochlon kai epebalon epʼ auton tas cheiras,

paragraphs.text: crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man that teacheth all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place; and moreover he brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath defiled this holy place.
paragraphs.original: κράζοντες· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, βοηθεῖτε· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ κατὰ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τοῦ τόπου τούτου πάντας πανταχῇ διδάσκων, ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ κεκοίνωκεν τὸν ἅγιον τόπον τοῦτον.
paragraphs.translit: krazontes· Andres Israēlitai, boētheite· houtos estin ho anthrōpos ho kata tou laou kai tou nomou kai tou topou toutou pantas pantachē didaskōn, eti te kai Hellēnas eisēgagen eis to hieron kai kekoinōken ton hagion topon touton.

paragraphs.text: For they had before seen with him in the city Trophimus the Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν γὰρ προεωρακότες Τρόφιμον τὸν Ἐφέσιον ἐν τῇ πόλει σὺν αὐτῷ, ὃν ἐνόμιζον ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν εἰσήγαγεν ὁ Παῦλος.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan gar proeōrakotes Trophimon ton Ephesion en tē polei syn autō, hon enomizon hoti eis to hieron eisēgagen ho Paulos.

paragraphs.text: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together; and they laid hold on Paul, and dragged him out of the temple: and straightway the doors were shut.
paragraphs.original: ἐκινήθη τε ἡ πόλις ὅλη καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενοι τοῦ Παύλου εἷλκον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι.
paragraphs.translit: ekinēthē te hē polis holē kai egeneto syndromē tou laou, kai epilabomenoi tou Paulou heilkon auton exō tou hierou, kai eutheōs ekleisthēsan hai thyrai.

paragraphs.text: And as they were seeking to kill him, tidings came up to the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in confusion.
paragraphs.original: ζητούντων τε αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀνέβη φάσις τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης ὅτι ὅλη συγχύννεται Ἰερουσαλήμ,
paragraphs.translit: zētountōn te auton apokteinai anebē phasis tō chiliarchō tēs speirēs hoti holē synchynnetai Ierousalēm,

paragraphs.text: And forthwith he took soldiers and centurions, and ran down upon them: and they, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, left off beating Paul.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἐξαυτῆς παραλαβὼν στρατιώτας καὶ ἑκατοντάρχας κατέδραμεν ἐπʼ αὐτούς, οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας ἐπαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον.
paragraphs.translit: hos exautēs paralabōn stratiōtas kai hekatontarchas katedramen epʼ autous, hoi de idontes ton chiliarchon kai tous stratiōtas epausanto typtontes ton Paulon.

paragraphs.text: Then the chief captain came near, and laid hold on him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and inquired who he was, and what he had done.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἐγγίσας ὁ χιλίαρχος ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκέλευσε δεθῆναι ἁλύσεσι δυσί, καὶ ἐπυνθάνετο τίς εἴη καὶ τί ἐστιν πεποιηκώς.
paragraphs.translit: tote engisas ho chiliarchos epelabeto autou kai ekeleuse dethēnai halysesi dysi, kai epynthaneto tis eiē kai ti estin pepoiēkōs.

paragraphs.text: And some shouted one thing, some another, among the crowd: and when he could not know the certainty for the uproar, he commanded him to be brought into the castle.
paragraphs.original: ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι ἐπεφώνουν ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ· μὴ δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸν θόρυβον ἐκέλευσεν ἄγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.
paragraphs.translit: alloi de allo ti epephōnoun en tō ochlō· mē dynamenou de autou gnōnai to asphales dia ton thorybon ekeleusen agesthai auton eis tēn parembolēn.

paragraphs.text: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the crowd;
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀναβαθμούς, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ τὴν βίαν τοῦ ὄχλου,
paragraphs.translit: hote de egeneto epi tous anabathmous, synebē bastazesthai auton hypo tōn stratiōtōn dia tēn bian tou ochlou,

paragraphs.text: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, Away with him.
paragraphs.original: ἠκολούθει γὰρ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ κράζοντες· Αἶρε αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ēkolouthei gar to plēthos tou laou krazontes· Aire auton.

paragraphs.text: And as Paul was about to be brought into the castle, he saith unto the chief captain, May I say something unto thee? And he said, Dost thou know Greek?
paragraphs.original: Μέλλων τε εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τῷ χιλιάρχῳ· Εἰ ἔξεστίν μοι εἰπεῖν τι πρὸς σέ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἑλληνιστὶ γινώσκεις;
paragraphs.translit: Mellōn te eisagesthai eis tēn parembolēn ho Paulos legei tō chiliarchō· Ei exestin moi eipein ti pros se; ho de ephē· Hellēnisti ginōskeis;

paragraphs.text: Art thou not then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος ὁ πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστατώσας καὶ ἐξαγαγὼν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους ἄνδρας τῶν σικαρίων;
paragraphs.translit: ouk ara sy ei ho Aigyptios ho pro toutōn tōn hēmerōn anastatōsas kai exagagōn eis tēn erēmon tous tetrakischilious andras tōn sikariōn;

paragraphs.text: But Paul said, I am a Jew, of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and I beseech thee, give me leave to speak unto the people.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος· Ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος μέν εἰμι Ἰουδαῖος, Ταρσεὺς τῆς Κιλικίας, οὐκ ἀσήμου πόλεως πολίτης· δέομαι δέ σου, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho Paulos· Egō anthrōpos men eimi Ioudaios, Tarseus tēs Kilikias, ouk asēmou poleōs politēs· deomai de sou, epitrepson moi lalēsai pros ton laon.

paragraphs.text: And when he had given him leave, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with the hand unto the people; and when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew language, saying,
paragraphs.original: ἐπιτρέψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν κατέσεισε τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ, πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης προσεφώνησεν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ λέγων
paragraphs.translit: epitrepsantos de autou ho Paulos hestōs epi tōn anabathmōn kateseise tē cheiri tō laō, pollēs de sigēs genomenēs prosephōnēsen tē Hebraidi dialektō legōn
